Living hope requires changed conduct and sincere love during present trials

Verses 18–19 say the readers were redeemed with the blood of Christ. Verse 22 says they have purified their souls by obeying the truth. That purifying has an aim stated in the verse: sincere brotherly affection. Then the command follows: love one another from the heart, fervently. Verse 23 gives the ground for it. They were born again of seed that does not perish. Verses 24–25 contrast that with grass, which withers.
A shared spiritual house stands beside unequal power and the refusal of revenge

Verse 18 tells servants to submit even to harsh masters. Verse 20 says there is no credit in bearing a deserved beating. Bearing unjust suffering is what God commends. Verse 21 gives Christ as the example for that case. Verse 23 says what he did not do: he did not curse back or threaten. He entrusted himself to the one who judges justly. Verse 24 adds that he bore our sins in his body on the tree.
Shared inheritance and gentle witness frame the argument about suffering and rescue

Verse 15 tells them to be ready with an answer about their hope. It adds the manner: with humility and fear. Verse 16 adds a third condition, a good conscience. The reason is practical. They are being spoken against as evildoers. A good way of life disappoints those who curse it. Verse 17 says suffering for doing good is better than for doing evil.
Changed conduct needs shared service when former companions respond with insults

Verse 4 says former companions now speak evil of the readers. The next verses turn to life inside the group. Verse 8 asks for earnest love, and verse 9 for hospitality without grumbling. Verse 10 gives the rule for every member. Each has received a gift and is to use it to serve others. The verse calls them managers of God’s grace, which takes many forms. Verse 11 names two kinds of gift: speaking and serving.
Leadership by example and shared humility answer danger without ruling through fear

Verse 2 gives three contrasts for elders, and verse 3 is the third. They serve willingly, not under pressure. They serve eagerly, not for dishonest gain. They lead by example, not by lording it over the flock. The flock is called “those entrusted to you,” so it is not theirs. Verse 4 names the chief Shepherd, who will appear. Verse 5 then asks humility of everyone, elders included.
